July 19 (UPI) -- Extensive search and rescue missions were underway in Peru's mountainous central Andean highlands Sunday following a deadly 5.1 magnitude earthquake.

The Peruvian National Police said they were actively conducting search, rescue, emergency response and security operations in the Junin region after Saturday's temblor, which had its epicenter in the Chongos Bajo district of Chupaca province, about 200 miles east of Lima.

More than 250 personnel from the Peru's emergency services, K-9 and medical units, as well as other specialized teams, were also in the rugged highlands as the government issued a preliminary report of five dead, 21 injured and more than 300 affected by the quake.

.@Sismos_Peru_IGP informa sismo de magnitud 5.1 con epicentro en Chongos Bajo, Chupaca - Junín. pic.twitter.com/IDInn6MPEy— COEN - INDECI (@COENPeru) July 19, 2026

It struck at 9:21 p.m. Saturday local time.

"I deeply regret the consequences of the earthquake that occurred in Junín," Peruvian President-elect Keiko Fujimori said in a statement. "I express my most heartfelt condolences to the families of those who have passed away and my solidarity with those who have been affected."

The national volunteer firefighting corps were similarly dispatched to the region to aid the National Police in search and rescue operations, debris removal, evacuations and pre-hospital care for those in the hardest-hit areas, the interior ministry said.

The health ministry, meanwhile, sent a brigade of specialists brigade to begin providing medical care to those affected, joining local teams already present in Junin.

"The Ministry of Health maintains continuous monitoring of the emergency and will continue to mobilize the human, logistical, and medical resources necessary to safeguard the lives and health of the affected population," officials said.
